items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: We had on trumpet. Howard. Yes, Howard was on trumpet.

ctx.x: On 6th Street or 5th Street. That was in Cincinnati. Uh, we played there about six weeks or eight weeks. That was a whole band? Yeah, that was a whole band. We had, uh... We had on trumpet. Howard. Yes, Howard was on trumpet. And then we had, uh, this is a crippled trombone player there. Because Jim had taken the sick and they got him to work in his place. Oh, he plays with... He was playing with Bob Bob, Brandon, all the time.
Oh, I know what you mean by Derek, or Bob, Frog.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: Then after that we had Kid Howard with us. Oh yeah. Well he made several trips out there with us.

ctx.x: Then after that we had Kid Howard with us. Oh yeah. Well he made several trips out there with us. Tom Jefferson he worked out there with us. Yeah. Then we had him in Frisco, we had Howard in Frisco too. Well they were switching about you know. Yeah, yeah.
The first trumpet player that you had in George's band then was El Morroco Talbot.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: I said, as long as you got me in drag, your band will never be broke up. No. But I said, as far as getting another man, I said, I'm more than sure you can get somebody to replace Jim and Howard.

ctx.x: Sure, they'd like to have the whole band.

Yeah, you see, but just like the band, I'm sure. Just like he said that they working this deal like they did before, bringing him over first and then bringing the band over afterwards, you know. So he was on the impression that his band was going to be broke up. I said, no, I said, as long as you got me in drag, your band will never be broke up. No. But I said, as far as getting another man, I said, I'm more than sure you can get somebody to replace Jim and Howard.
Yes, Jim doesn't want to travel much anymore.
